seen_animation: A black-line mallet (rectangular head with an open left corner and rounded top-right corner, a handle with a square binding near its lower end and a short pointed stub past the binding) sits in front of grey scenery: a horizon line, a slanted line at left, a tree trunk at right and zigzag grass at the bottom. In frames 1-2 the mallet lies nearly horizontal at lower centre, head upright on the right, handle pointing left. In frames 3-5 it rotates and rises so the head swings up and to the right. From frame 5 to 10 it holds at a 45-degree diagonal with the head upper right against the trunk. In frame 11 it turns to a near-upright pose with the head tilted and set further left, and it holds that pose through frame 16. Throughout, the pointed stub stays near horizontal while the handle above the binding is diagonal, so the handle bends at the binding.
seen_film: A bearded caveman sits on a rock in front of a cave wall holding a club made of a bundle of sticks tied to a black stone. In frame 1 he is bent forward striking the stone down at lower right. In frames 2-3 he sits up fast (smear/double exposure) and raises the club to an upright-diagonal position at the right with the stone at upper right, and puts his other hand to his forehead. Frames 4-8 hold this pose with only small head changes. In frames 9-10 he lowers the hand to his mouth (smears) and brings the club slightly inward. In frames 11-16 he holds the club more upright in front of his chest with both hands, the stone near head height, and looks at it with a dejected face; this pose holds to the end.
named_subject: A hand mallet/hammer (the club the caveman holds), drawn as the doodle in c.png with an added binding and stub at the handle end.
evidence: The overall path matches the film: e.png 1 the mallet is low at lower centre-right where the film's club strikes the rock (f.png 1); it ends high-right at a diagonal (e.png 8-24, film f.png 6-20) and then turns more upright in front of the trunk (e.png 25-38, film f.png 26-38). Timing at the start lags: in f.png 2-4 the club is already raised upright beside the face, while in e.png 2-4 the mallet is still nearly horizontal and low; it only reaches the raised diagonal at e.png 7-8, about 4 frames late. The second turn is a pop: e.png 24 is the 45-degree diagonal with the head against the trunk, e.png 25 is already the near-upright pose with the head shifted left and down by roughly a head width, with no in-between, while the film spends f.png 21-26 moving the club inward through smear frames. During the long hold (e.png 8-24) the mallet is completely frozen while the film's club stays nearly still too, so that hold is acceptable. g.png shows a continuous rise from 1 to 7, a tight cluster for the hold, then a single displaced group for 25 onward. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The second action (club turned from the raised diagonal to upright in front of the chest) happens in one frame between e.png 24 and 25 instead of over the 4-6 frames the film uses, and the initial lift starts about 3-4 frames after the film's lift.
closes_when: The mallet is already near the raised diagonal by e.png 3-4, and e.png 21-26 show the head moving progressively left and down and the handle rotating toward vertical in steps of similar size, with no single-frame change larger than its neighbours.
protect: The mallet head's construction from c.png (open left corner stroke, rounded top-right corner, slight kink where handle meets head); consistent size across all frames; the overall placement (low at the rock at start, high-right against the trunk mid-shot, upright in front of the trunk at the end); the smooth rotation in e.png 3-7; the still holds that match the film's holds.
identity_gap: The head matches c.png, but the handle is not the doodle's single straight handle with a rounded end: it is shortened, carries an added square binding, and ends in a pointed stub that stays horizontal while the handle above it is diagonal, so the handle bends at a joint the doodle does not have.
